editorial.headline: Egg Wholesale, With Bali’s PMA Door Closed
editorial.standfirst: This activity is nationally open to PMA, but Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium blocks its PMA registration today.
editorial.body:
For a foreign investor, the defining fact about KBLI 46325 in Bali is straightforward: it cannot be registered for PMA there today. That conclusion does not change the national classification. Nationally, the activity is open to PMA and carries a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. But Bali applies a separate island-wide, permanent moratorium to PMA registration for every Low- and Medium-Low-risk KBLI. For this activity, the recorded OSS risk at the Besar scale is Low/Medium-Low across every scope, bringing it inside that Bali restriction. The result is a genuine split between national openness and Bali registration reality.

The commercial subject is wholesale trade in eggs and processed egg products. It is an activity defined by the circulation of these goods through wholesale channels, with eggs and egg products belonging together in the stated scope. That simple description matters: the code’s centre of gravity is the wholesale market for a specific food category. A clear internal description should keep that focus intact—eggs and their processed products, traded at wholesale—rather than allowing the activity to become a vague label for the wider food economy. In regulatory terms, scope is the boundary of what the code says it includes.

The national opening is not reserved for only one end of the business spectrum. The recorded scales open to this activity are Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That gives the code a broad formal scale range for businesses registering it. For PMA planning, the point is equally clear at the national level: the 100% ceiling means foreign ownership may reach the full shareholding position permitted by the record. The national basis cited is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. None of that national position removes Bali’s local PMA constraint.

Bali’s status is Blocked (risk class): blocked on the activity’s risk class. The stated reason is specific: at the Besar scale, every scope is assessed in OSS as Low or Medium-Low risk, and the Bali moratorium consequently blocks PMA registration. The moratorium is recorded as applying from May 13, 2026, across the province on a permanent basis. This nationally open activity is blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the stated moratorium.
